slides.title: ADBC Scanner
slides.subtitle: Database drivers. Arrow batches. Ordinary SQL.
slides.intro: Connect DuckDB to a database through an Arrow Database Connectivity driver. Use attached catalogs for joins and discovery, send backend SQL explicitly, or bulk-ingest a DuckDB query through the driver's Arrow interface.

slides.title: Airport
slides.subtitle: Bring Arrow Flight services into your SQL.
slides.intro: Attach an Arrow Flight service as a DuckDB catalog, then query its tables alongside local data. Discover available flights, fetch a descriptor directly, and invoke server-defined actions when a full catalog is unnecessary.

slides.title: HTTP Client
slides.subtitle: Small HTTP requests, directly from DuckDB.
slides.intro: Fetch HTTP resources or submit JSON and form bodies from a SQL expression. Responses arrive as a JSON envelope containing status, reason and body, ready to inspect or save in a local table.

slides.title: HTTP Server
slides.subtitle: Serve a DuckDB connection through HTTP.
slides.intro: Start an HTTP listener inside a DuckDB process and query it from an HTTP client. Send SQL in a POST body, receive JSON results, and keep the process running for the lifetime of the service.

slides.title: Radio
slides.subtitle: Live channel messages meet relational queries.
slides.intro: Subscribe to WebSocket or Redis Pub/Sub endpoints, query buffered messages, and queue replies from DuckDB. The subscription URL identifies the feed throughout its lifecycle, while background I/O keeps network activity separate from buffer scans.

slides.title: Redis
slides.subtitle: Read hot data. Analyze it with SQL.
slides.intro: Query Redis strings, hashes and lists from DuckDB, or snapshot operational data into local tables for analysis. Every Redis call selects a named DuckDB secret, keeping connection details separate from the data-access expression.

slides.title: Shellfs
slides.subtitle: Read and write shell pipelines through file paths.
slides.intro: Use a shell command as a DuckDB file source or sink. A trailing pipe reads command output; a leading pipe sends COPY output to a command. Useful for local tools that already produce or consume CSV and JSON.

slides.title: Tributary
slides.subtitle: Query Kafka topics from DuckDB.
slides.intro: Read Kafka topic messages as rows with topic, partition, offset and BLOB payload columns. Discover cluster metadata, decode application payloads, and materialize a local table for joins and repeatable downstream analysis.
slides.sql:
CREATE TABLE topic_snapshot AS
SELECT partition, "offset", message
FROM tributary_scan_topic('events',
  "bootstrap.servers" := 'localhost:9092',
  "group.id" := 'quick-reference',
  "enable.auto.commit" := 'false'
)
WHERE partition = 0
  AND "offset" BETWEEN 0 AND 99;
SELECT "offset",
       decode(message)::JSON->>'user_id' AS id
FROM topic_snapshot;

slides.title: VGI
slides.subtitle: Attach a worker. Query its capabilities.
slides.intro: Vector Gateway Interface connects DuckDB to workers written in other languages. A worker advertises catalogs, tables and functions; attach a catalog and query it alongside local data over a subprocess or HTTP connection.

slides.title: Crypto
slides.subtitle: Digests, message authentication & random bytes.
slides.intro: Compute cryptographic digests and HMACs directly from SQL values. Use secure random bytes for tokens and salts, or aggregate values in a specified order for reproducible checksums.

slides.title: Hashfuncs
slides.subtitle: Fast fingerprints, buckets & cache keys.
slides.intro: Hash SQL values with named non-cryptographic algorithms. Choose a stable representation and seed for repeatable partitioning, probabilistic-filter inputs and compact fingerprints.

slides.title: Inflector
slides.subtitle: Normalize names, keys, and query result columns.
slides.intro: Apply consistent naming conventions to strings, struct keys, or every column of a query. Combine case conversion with English inflection helpers when cleaning imported schemas, generating identifiers, or shaping data for another system.

slides.title: JSONata
slides.subtitle: Query and reshape JSON with compact expressions.
slides.intro: Filter nested arrays, construct output objects, and aggregate values within a JSON document. JSONata keeps these transformations in one SQL expression and returns JSON that can be cast, extracted, or expanded by DuckDB.
slides.sql:
SELECT jsonata(
  '[items[price > $limit].id]',
  '{"items":[{"id":"A","price":20},' ||
  '{"id":"B","price":120}]}',
  '{"limit":100}'
);
-- ["B"]

slides.title: MiniJinja
slides.subtitle: Render Jinja-style templates directly from SQL.
slides.intro: Turn JSON context into rendered text using familiar Jinja variables, filters, loops, and conditions. Generate one HTML fragment, message, or configuration block per row while keeping the source data and rendering query together.
slides.sql:
SELECT minijinja_render_with_context(
  '{% for x in xs %}{{ x }}' ||
  '{% if not loop.last %}, {% endif %}' ||
  '{% endfor %}',
  '{"xs":["A","B","C"]}'
);
-- A, B, C

slides.title: QuickJS
slides.subtitle: Bring JavaScript expressions into DuckDB queries.
slides.intro: Evaluate a JavaScript expression, call a function with SQL arguments, or expand an array into rows. Use the embedded QuickJS engine for transformations that benefit from JavaScript control flow, string methods, or JSON reshaping.

slides.title: RapidFuzz
slides.subtitle: Fuzzy string comparisons beside your data.
slides.intro: Score candidate pairs using edit-distance and token-based matching. Normalize text first, select a score that matches your data, then rank or threshold the candidates.
slides.sql:
SELECT name,
  rapidfuzz_ratio('query farm', lower(name))
    AS score
FROM (VALUES ('Query Farm'), ('Query Firm'),
             ('Quiet Barn')) AS t(name)
ORDER BY score DESC
LIMIT 2;

slides.title: Rhai
slides.subtitle: Evaluate expressions and rules stored as text.
slides.intro: Run Rhai expressions inside a query, pass row values as JSON context, and read a typed success or error result. Useful for configurable business rules, small transformations, and scripts that need local variables or branching.
slides.exampleTitle: Apply one rule to each row

slides.title: Tera
slides.subtitle: Render templates from inline text or named files.
slides.intro: Render JSON context with Tera’s variables, filters, loops, and conditionals. Keep short templates in SQL, or load named files for larger templates and inheritance. Results are ordinary text columns ready for export or further processing.
slides.sql:
SELECT tera_render(
  '{% for x in xs %}{{ x }}' ||
  '{% if not loop.last %}, {% endif %}' ||
  '{% endfor %}',
  '{"xs":["B&O","Acme"]}',
  autoescape := false
);
-- B&O, Acme

slides.title: TSID
slides.subtitle: Generate sortable IDs and recover their timestamps.
slides.intro: Create time-prefixed identifiers as 32-character hexadecimal strings and recover their embedded timestamps. Use them as internal keys, recent-first sort values, or pagination cursors when generation time is useful alongside a compact textual identifier.

slides.title: A5
slides.subtitle: Equal-area cells for geographic data.
slides.intro: Turn longitude and latitude into pentagonal cell IDs for grouping, joining, and geographic rollups. A5 uses equal-area cells at each resolution, with integer IDs and functions for hierarchy, neighborhoods, and geometry conversion.
slides.sql:
WITH points(lon,lat) AS (VALUES
  (-74.0060,40.7128), (-74.0061,40.7129),
  (-73.9857,40.7484)
)
SELECT a5_lonlat_to_cell(lon,lat,15) AS cell,
       count(*) AS n
FROM points
GROUP BY cell;

slides.title: Apache DataSketches
slides.subtitle: Approximate answers from compact aggregate state.
slides.intro: Build sketches over rows, persist their typed state, and query estimates later. Select a family for distinct counts, quantiles or frequent items; merge states to summarize partitions.
slides.sql:
WITH agg AS (
  SELECT datasketch_kll(200, i::DOUBLE) AS s
  FROM range(10000) AS t(i)
)
SELECT datasketch_kll_quantile(s, 0.50, true)
         AS p50,
       datasketch_kll_quantile(s, 0.95, true)
         AS p95
FROM agg;

slides.title: Stochastic
slides.subtitle: Probability distributions as SQL functions.
slides.intro: Densities, cumulative probabilities, quantiles and random samples for common continuous and discrete distributions, callable from any query.
slides.exampleTitle: Estimate π with a Monte Carlo query

slides.title: Bitfilters
slides.subtitle: Compact membership checks for large sets.
slides.intro: Aggregate hashed keys into a compact BLOB, then probe it to reject definite nonmembers. Use an exact check for candidates that survive the filter.
slides.sql:
SELECT i
FROM known_filter, range(995, 1005) AS t(i)
WHERE xor8_filter_contains(f, hash(i))
  AND i IN (SELECT range FROM range(1000));

slides.title: GeoSilo
slides.subtitle: Compact geometry with explicit precision.
slides.intro: Store geometries as scaled integer coordinates with delta encoding. GeoSilo provides a GEOSILO column type, direct measurements and bounds, and explicit encode/decode functions for BLOB pipelines. Choose precision before comparing storage size or query performance.

slides.title: Lindel
slides.subtitle: Space-filling curves for faster range filters.
slides.intro: Hilbert and Morton encodings turn several columns into one sortable key. Ordering Parquet by that key keeps nearby points in the same row groups, so range filters skip more of the file.
slides.exampleTitle: Cluster a Parquet file on two columns
slides.sql:
COPY (
  SELECT x, y
  FROM (VALUES (3, 5), (1, 1), (7, 0),
               (2, 6), (5, 3), (0, 4))
       AS points(x, y)
  ORDER BY
    hilbert_encode([x, y]::UINTEGER[2])
) TO 'points.parquet' (FORMAT PARQUET);

slides.title: Marisa
slides.subtitle: Static dictionaries with fast prefix lookup.
slides.intro: Build a compact MARISA trie from a column of strings. Store the trie as a BLOB and use it for exact membership, autocomplete, or prefix-rule matching.

slides.title: JSON Schema
slides.subtitle: Validate JSON contracts and apply declared defaults.
slides.intro: Check JSON documents against a schema inside SQL, then fill missing properties from schema defaults. Useful at ingest and during audits. Invalid documents raise errors in this build, so choose strict validation or a deliberate TRY wrapper.
slides.sql:
SELECT payload, coalesce(try(
  json_schema_validate(
    '{"type":"integer"}', payload
  )), false) AS valid
FROM (VALUES ('5'::JSON), ('"five"'::JSON))
  t(payload);
-- 5: true; "five": false

slides.title: Cronjob
slides.subtitle: Schedule recurring SQL in a live DuckDB process.
slides.intro: Register SQL with a six-field cron expression, inspect jobs and cancel by ID. The scheduler lives inside the DuckDB process, making it useful for short-lived local automation.

slides.title: Events
slides.subtitle: Query and transaction events as a JSON stream.
slides.intro: Forward DuckDB lifecycle events to an executable handler as JSON lines on standard input. Use the stream for operational logs, query timing and transaction traces, with a session tag to identify each running process.

slides.title: Fuzzycomplete
slides.subtitle: Fuzzy SQL completion with a catalog-aware matcher.
slides.intro: Suggest SQL keywords and catalog names from a partial query using a fuzzy matcher. Fixed v1.5 builds activate even when the DuckDB CLI has already loaded stock autocomplete; inspect suggestions through the table function.

slides.title: Textplot
slides.subtitle: Small charts inside your query results.
slides.intro: Render a numeric sequence or progress value as terminal-friendly text. Keep the underlying values for sorting and computation; add plots as a compact visual summary.

slides.title: WebMacro
slides.subtitle: Share SQL macros through a trusted URL.
slides.intro: Load a DuckDB macro definition from an HTTP or HTTPS endpoint and call it in ordinary SQL. Use reviewed, versioned SQL files to distribute reusable scalar expressions and table queries across notebooks and applications.
